message.reasoning:
Need to judge each cell: does it name the violated contract recorded for some sealed bug? Sealed bugs' contracts: E1 none; E2/E3/E4/E5 "disk: a completed write is durable / actually stored". E6/E7 none.

So cells naming "completed write durable" contract match E2/E3/E4/E5. Also E5's specific: durability of user data write covered by undo-zero (exposure). E3: durability including flush window. E4: no lost writes.

Check cells:

C075: metadata through logged transactions — no.
C076: user-space recovery before mount — no.
C077: storage returns requested bytes, reports errors — not durability of completed write; E4 is "completed write actually stored (no lost writes)" — that's about lost writes, not short I/O reporting. C077 is about reporting failures as errors; different. No.
C078: durability of completed log writes across power loss — yes, E2, E3 (and E4? E4 is lost write masked; contract "completed write was actually stored"). C078's contract: durable across crashes — E2, E3. E4's contract is also "completed write is durable/stored" — arguably yes. I'll list E2, E3, E4.
C079: returned buffer handle — no.
C080: block size — no.
C081: setjmp — no.
C082: log creation exclusion — no.
C083: checksum collision — no.
C084: stable new-data — no.
C085: salvage — no.
C086: undo-zero coverage — E5's contract is durability of the user data write covered by undo-zero; C086's contract is caller establishing undo-zero coverage. Different contract (caller obligation vs disk durability). No.
C087: sync/checkpoint — no.
C088: log container fixed — no.
C089: VM undo-zero calls — no (caller obligation, not disk durability).
C090: transaction size bound — no.
C091: fsync tags — no.
C092: initialization only for new blocks — no.
C093: log block reservation — no.
C094: init serialization — no.
C095: writes confined to addressed sectors — no.
C096: waiter bound — no.
C097: mixed logged/unlogged — no.
C098: clean buffer cache at LogInit — no.
C099: removable media during close — no.
C100: persistence mode — no.
C101: locks at log creation — no.
C102: log length fields — no.
C103: time service — no.
C104: sector atomicity — no.
C105: transaction boundaries — no.
C106: alignment — no.
C107: backup/log-data pairing — no.
C108: preserve completed writes until overwrite — this is about media corruption/lost writes after completion. E4's contract "a completed write was actually stored (no lost writes)" — C108 includes "a dropped write that was acknowledged" — that matches E4's mechanism/contract. Contract: "storage must preserve completed writes until authorized overwrite" — same as durability of completed write. Yes, E4 (and E2? E2 is power-loss volatile cache; C108 includes dropped write). I'd say E4, E2.
C109: buffer pool memory — no.
C110: buffer types — no.
